title: Graceful degradation for partial structured streams and tool retry policies
creator: Amara Patel
description: Problem: Clients using streamed structured responses + tool/function calling experience brittle failures when the model emits partial or malformed fragments, the tool invocation fails mid-stream, or when downstream services are flaky. This ticket captures acceptance criteria and edge-case behaviors for graceful degradation, observability, and deterministic retry semantics for tool calls. Goal: define a stable contract that SDKs/clients, runtime, and tool integrations can implement so production services can rely on consistent error envelopes, deterministic retries, and clear QA checks for partial/streamed payloads. This PRD focuses on required behaviors (schemas, error envelopes, streaming partials), testable acceptance criteria, and operational observability requirements. Non-goals: full SDK implementation and migration of existing customers; those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Streamed partial payloads: When the runtime streams structured output (e.g., interleaved JSON objects), receivers must be able to parse and recover from partial JSON fragments. The platform must emit a framing prefix ("chunk-type") for each chunk: 'schema', 'partial', 'complete', 'error', 'tool-call', 'tool-result'.

Schema guidance: If a model emits a 'schema' chunk at stream start, the schema must be syntactically valid JSON Schema draft-07 compatible JSON. If schema is absent, SDKs should fall back to 'best-effort' parsing and mark the response as 'schema-missing' in traces.

Partial-object semantics: 'partial' chunks contain syntactically valid JSON fragments with a stable continuation token. Consumers must concatenate fragments in-order using the continuation token and validate final object on 'complete' chunk. The runtime must provide a maximum fragment reassembly window of 30s before marking as 'fragment_timeout'.

Error envelope: All runtime/SDK errors occurring mid-stream must be delivered in a standard error envelope chunk with fields: error_code, message, severity (warning|recoverable|fatal), downstream_action (retry|fallback|abort). These must be documented and observable as tags in traces.

Tool-call handshake: For tool/function calls initiated from the model, the platform must produce a 'tool-call' chunk containing a tool_id, call_id (UUID), input_schema (optional), and idempotency_key. The platform must record call_id and idempotency_key for at least 7 days to support deduplication and replay protection.

Tool failure modes and retries: If a tool invocation returns a transient error (HTTP 5xx, network timeout), the platform will apply exponential backoff with jitter and attempt up to 3 retries unless the tool returns explicit 'do_not_retry' error. Retry attempts must preserve idempotency_key; if the tool is non-idempotent, platform must route to a 'synchronous-fallback' policy and include downstream_action: fallback in the error envelope.

Deterministic fallback: If a tool is permanently unavailable (e.g., 4xx auth errors), runtime must send a 'tool-result' chunk with status 'failed' and include a canonical fallback_result (if configured) or a structured error indicating fallback_unavailable. Client SDKs must surface fallback decisions to application callbacks so product logic can choose to retry or abort.

Backpressure: The platform must indicate backpressure via a 'flow_control' stream chunk when downstream processing lags. SDKs must honor flow_control hints for at least 5s before resuming normal read rates. Backpressure events must increment a metric 'stream.flow_control.count'.

Observability: Each stream must emit correlating identifiers: request_id, session_id (if present), and top-level model_version. Errors, tool_calls, retries, and fragment_timeouts must be logged as span events with tags matching the error envelope fields.
QA-verifiable outcomes: For every acceptance criterion above there must be at least one automated integration test that asserts both success and failure paths (see QA test cases).
qa_test_cases: Basic successful stream: model emits 'schema' then several 'partial' chunks then 'complete'. Assert parsed object matches schema and no error chunks emitted.

Malformed fragment recovery: simulate truncated partial chunk; runtime should emit 'error' chunk with severity 'recoverable' and clients should retry parse until reassembly times out; assert 'fragment_timeout' is emitted after 30s window.

Tool transient failure: tool returns HTTP 502 for first two attempts then 200. Assert platform retried twice, preserved idempotency_key, and client received single logical 'tool-result' with the final payload and 2 retry trace events.

Tool non-idempotent detected: tool returns header X-Non-Idempotent: true. Platform must stop automatic retries and return error envelope with downstream_action: fallback. Assert fallback_result delivered if configured.
Permanent tool auth failure: simulate 401. Assert platform emits 'tool-result' with status 'failed' and error_code 'tool_auth', and SDK surfaces fallback decision to the app layer.
Backpressure signal: Introduce artificial processing delay in client; assert platform sends 'flow_control' chunk and metric 'stream.flow_control.count' increments, SDK respects 5s honor period.
Observability traces: For each scenario assert spans include request_id, call_id, retry_count and error_code tags and that logs contain the canonical error envelope JSON.
Stress test: 1k concurrent streams with intermittent tool outages; validate no more than 1% fatal stream errors and that retries do not exceed configured global retry budget.
non_goals: Ship SDK-side automatic remediation UX changes—this ticket only defines server/runtime contract and acceptance tests.
Change existing customer contracts or migrate their existing tool integrations—those are separate migrations.
Designing new tool authentication protocols (KMS/HSM) as part of this scope.
dependencies: DES-411 (console: stream visualizer for partial fragments)
PM-45200 (policy: global retry budget and configuration)
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding a rigid schema vs. best-effort parsing — we choose optional schema announcement + runtime heuristics to avoid breaking existing customers.
Security consideration: idempotency_key retention window must balance dedupe usefulness with PII minimization—store keys but avoid storing full payloads.
We prefer explicit flow_control signals over dynamic TCP heuristics to keep client behavior deterministic.
This approach is intentionally conservative on retries to avoid amplifying downstream outages; global retry budget will be enforced by ENG-45200.
